questions.question: The two essential clauses in the definition of mass movement are:
options: Movement downslope under GRAVITY, and NO transporting agent such as a river, glacier or wind
Movement by wind, and only during storms
Movement uphill, and only of solid rock
Movement by rivers, and only in mountains

questions.question: The forces holding a slope together include:
options: Gravity and slope angle
Friction, the interlocking of grains, dry cohesion and plant ROOTS knitting the soil
Heavy rainfall and leaking pipes
Blasting and earthquakes

questions.question: Water plays a double game on slopes because:
options: It always strengthens soil in any amount
It only matters when frozen
A little moisture pulls grains together, but SATURATION pushes them apart, adds weight and greases potential slide surfaces
It evaporates before reaching the soil

questions.question: A road cutting sliced through the toe of a slope is dangerous because it:
options: Adds weight to the crest
Increases the friction in the soil
Waters the slope during storms
Removes the SUPPORT that was holding up everything above it

questions.question: Field evidence of soil creep includes:
options: Leaning fence posts and gravestones, tree trunks curved at the base, terracettes, and soil banked against the upslope side of walls
A crescent scar with a back-tilted block
A steel net full of shattered boulders
A valley floor of set mud

questions.question: Solifluction happens where:
options: Dry sand slides down a dune face
A thawed, waterlogged surface layer cannot drain and flows slowly in lobes over the FROZEN subsoil, as on the high Maloti and Drakensberg plateaus
Waves undercut a coastal cliff
Lava flows over a plain

questions.question: What separates a slump from an ordinary landslide is that the slump:
options: Is completely dry
Moves faster than sound
Fails along a CURVED, spoon-shaped surface, so the block ROTATES, leaving a crescent scar and a backward-tilted block
Only involves solid rock

questions.question: The deadliest and wettest of the six movements is the:
options: Soil creep
Solifluction lobe
Rock fall
MUD FLOW — debris saturated into a fluid that races down valleys and sets hard around what it catches

questions.question: Environmental impacts of mass movement include:
options: Slopes stripped to bedrock, fertile topsoil buried under rubble, and sediment choking rivers and silting dams
Faster-growing forests on the scar
Cleaner gravel beds for aquatic life
Deeper, more fertile soils everywhere

questions.question: In April 2022, parts of the Durban metro received:
options: No rain for six months
More than 300 mm of rain in 24 hours — several months' rainfall in a day — triggering hundreds of slope failures and more than 400 deaths
Light drizzle for a week
Heavy snowfalls

questions.question: Mass movement risk is socially unequal because:
options: Rain avoids wealthy suburbs
Steep land is always the most expensive
Poverty forces settlement onto steep, unstable slopes with hand-cut platforms, leaking water and no engineering
Informal settlements are only built on flat plains

questions.question: The Merriespruit disaster of 1994 near Virginia showed that:
options: Mud flows only occur in mountains
Earthquakes are South Africa's main slope trigger
Soil creep can destroy a town overnight
A rain-topped mine tailings dam can liquefy into a MUD FLOW that runs through the settlement below — saturation, slope and settlement in fatal alignment

questions.question: Gabions protect a slope by:
options: Supporting its TOE with wire cages packed with rock where support has been removed
Covering the crest with plastic sheeting
Draining the water table
Replacing the vegetation

questions.question: Controlling water on a slope means:
options: Aiming stormwater outlets at the slope face
Cut-off drains at the crest, perforated subsurface drains bleeding the slope, and rapid repair of leaks and cracks
Irrigating the slope in summer
Building a dam on the crest

questions.question: Vegetation is called engineering that grows because:
options: Trees block the view of the scar
Plants attract soil-compacting animals
Roots BIND the soil, canopies break the rain's force, and transpiration pumps water back out of the slope
Grass makes slopes steeper

questions.question: Planning-level defences include:
options: Building schools on the steepest available land
Cancelling all rainfall monitoring
Ignoring hazard maps once houses are built
GIS hazard mapping, zoning housing off red zones, rainfall-triggered evacuation warnings and community education on warning signs

questions.question: In the arm-wrestle picture, gravity's opponent is:
options: Friction, the grip of interlocked grains, and roots lacing the soil like the stitching in a rugby ball
Wind and waves
The weight of buildings
Sunlight warming the rock

questions.question: The rusk in the coffee shows that:
options: Soil is always weakest when bone dry
A brief dip leaves it firm — a little moisture binds — but a long soak makes it sag and let go, exactly like a saturated hillside
Water has no effect on soil strength
Only boiling water damages slopes

questions.question: Cutting a platform, clearing the grass and leaking pipe water into one hillside means:
options: The slope has been made safer three times over
Nothing changes until an earthquake strikes
People have weakened the slope three ways at once — support removed, roots gone, water added
Only the pipe matters

subtopics.title: The Six Speeds of Falling Ground

questions.question: The starting grid from slowest to fastest reads:
options: Creep, solifluction, landslide, slump, rock fall, mud flow
Mud flow, rock fall, slump, landslide, solifluction, creep
Creep, landslide, solifluction, mud flow, slump, rock fall
Slump, creep, mud flow, rock fall, landslide, solifluction

questions.question: Tree trunks curved at the base along a hillside are the trail of:
options: A recent rock fall
SOIL CREEP — the trees grow straight up while their footing slips slowly downhill
A mud flow
Solifluction in the lowveld

questions.question: The bricks shooting off a tipper truck when the bed tilts too far picture:
options: Soil creep
Solifluction
A LANDSLIDE — one coherent mass failing along a single surface, usually after soaking rain
A slump rotating on a spoon-shaped surface

questions.question: The trend along the grid is:
options: Speed falls as water rises
Water and speed are unrelated
All six lanes move at identical speed
Speed UP, water UP — from the slow dry tortoise of creep to the racing fluid mud flow

subtopics.title: April 2022 and How to Fight Back

questions.question: The sentence that turns the April 2022 case study from description into understanding is:
options: Same rain, unequal risk — the families with the least choice lived on the steepest, least protected slopes, and that is where the hills failed hardest
The rain fell only on the coast
Slopes in cities never fail
The disaster was caused by an earthquake

questions.question: Where rock falls cannot be prevented on mountain passes, engineers:
options: Close the pass permanently
CATCH the rock with anchored mesh and catch fences above the road
Remove the entire cliff
Paint warning lines on the cliff face

questions.question: The four fight-back moves are:
options: Watch, wait, warn, weep
Dig, dump, dam, drive
RESHAPE the slope, DRAIN the water, PLANT the surface, PLAN the settlement
Terrace, tar, tow, tunnel

questions.question: A slope whispers that it is preparing to fail through:
options: Dry, cracked river beds downstream
Even green grass across the whole hillside
Clear skies after rain
Fresh cracks, leaning poles, jamming doors and windows, and water seeping where it never seeped before
